Operator: Good day, and welcome to the AetherLink Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. For those on webcast, there will be a prompt to register your questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to AetherLink Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Network Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include substantial progress on 5G deployment reaching nationwide coverage milestones and CapEx investments supporting network leadership. We are also seeing substantial growth from our 5G fixed wireless access service with a significant surge in broadband subscribers. Further, we are concentrating on generating robust free cash flow to fuel deleveraging and shareholder returns. Additionally, our revenue mix shows increasing contributions from high-margin wireless and media segments. We are also improving profitability through targeted operating expense optimization initiatives. We are strategically investing in spectrum assets with high utilization and forward allocation plans. Finally, net subscriber additions are accelerating across residential and business segments, and our CapEx guidance for network investments remains disciplined.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $14.8 billion, representing a 7% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.4 billion, resulting in a margin of 36.5%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $2.8 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

To provide more depth on the key highlights Michael mentioned, let me start with our network investments, where we're advancing rapidly on our 5G transformation while optimizing spending for coverage superiority and returns. 5G forms the foundation for our integrated telecom and media approach, powering low-latency apps like 8K streaming, cloud gaming collaborations with Epic Games and Roblox, and private 5G setups for media studios.

On deployment progress, we hit a key milestone in Q3 with nationwide non-standalone 5G coverage at 95% of the U.S. population, up from 88% last year. Leveraging our sub-6GHz C-band spectrum from the 2021 FCC auction costing $4.6 billion, we're delivering median downloads of 350 Mbps, ahead of AT&T's 320 Mbps and competitive with T-Mobile. Standalone 5G reached 55% coverage, exceeding our 50% goal, enabling network slicing—such as our Ericsson dual-mode core partnership for Disney live sports trials with sub-10ms latency for AR during NFL games. In high-band, over 12,000 mmWave small cells are live in urban hubs like New York, LA, and Chicago, powering immersive experiences at venues like Dodger Stadium.

Urban areas stand at 99% NSA and SA coverage, with beamforming and massive MIMO up to 64T64R from Nokia lifting capacity 40% year-over-year. Rural coverage hit 85% via dynamic spectrum sharing on mid-band, supported by $500 million in Rural Digital Opportunity Fund grants. In Europe, our Vodafone JV covers 70% of London and Manchester with SA 5G, tied to BT Sport for EU-compliant low-latency broadcasts.

We're advancing Open RAN, with 25% of new sites using O-RAN gear from Nokia baseband, Samsung radios, and Altiostar vRAN, reducing costs 15% per site and enabling AWS Wavelength for media edge computing. We've refarmed 20% of 4G LTE spectrum to 5G, unlocking 200 MHz nationwide.

For CapEx, Q3 spend was $2.8 billion within our $2.6-2.9 billion range, YTD at $8.1 billion or 18% of revenue, flat year-over-year. Wireless took 65% or $1.8 billion: $1.2 billion on RAN/transport up 10% quarter-over-quarter for SA, $400 million on SAS licenses and mmWave backhaul, $200 million on fiber fronthaul. Site intensity dropped to $450K per macro down 12% via virtualized RAN and Amdocs AI tools. Fixed at 25% or $700 million expanded FTTH to 2.5 million homes, synergistic with 5G FWA adding 500K subs up 150% at $55 ARPU. Full-year 2024 guidance is $10.8-11.2 billion, trending to $10-10.5 billion in 2025 as efficiencies scale, supporting 48% EBITDA margins and strong ROI like 24-month urban payback and 15% IRR rural.

These moves position us for telecom-media convergence, monetizing enterprise private networks with $150 million NBCUniversal pilots and 20% uptake on 5G-streaming bundles. Our scale mitigates macro risks.

Next, on free cash flow, we generated $3.2 billion in Q3, up 18% year-over-year, with trailing twelve months at $12.8 billion, beating guidance. This reflects EBITDA growth to $8.7 billion up 12%, wireless service up 5% from 1.2 million postpaid adds and $68 ARPU on premium plans, FWA to 4.5 million up 45%, and streaming to 65 million subs up 8% with 1.9% churn via NFL rights and AI recommendations.

Working capital freed $450 million via vendor terms and spectrum optimizations. CapEx at $4.1 billion down 10% sequentially at 22% intensity, 60% to network: 35% mmWave/C-band, 15% Open RAN, 10% edge. North America drove 75% FCF at $2.4 billion, Europe 15% with Vodafone synergies, APAC 10%.

Utilization: 34% or $1.1 billion to deleveraging, net debt to $85 billion at 2.3x leverage. 28% or $900 million to dividends $0.65/share yielding 4.2% and $400 million buybacks under $10 billion program, 15 million shares YTD at $42 average for 12% FCF yield. 16% or $500 million to growth: $300 million FTTx, $200 million content M&A. Balance builds cash to $7.5 billion for auctions like 3.45-3.55 GHz.

FY2024 FCF guide $13.0-13.5 billion, with capex $16.5-17 billion.

Turning to revenue mix, total $14.8 billion up 7%: Wireless 48% or $7.1 billion up from 45%, service $6.2 billion up 9%, postpaid ARPU $52.30 up 4% on 5G covering 85%, 1.2 million adds including 450K SA and FWA. Broadband/Wireline 25% $3.7 billion up 12% fiber, FTTH 45 million homes, ARPU $68, $2.5 billion CapEx for XGS-PON. Media/Entertainment 18% $2.7 billion up 15%, TeleStream+ 28 million subs, AVOD $450 million up 25%, NFL integration. Enterprise 8% $1.2 billion up 11%, edge deals $300 million. Other 1% $150 million.

Mix shift +3 ppt to wireless/media reduces cyclicality, margins to 42%.

On operating expense management, Q3 opex $7.2 billion down 4.2% YoY, $312 million savings from Opex Optimization 2.0, organic deflation 5.1%, boosting EBITDA $428 million or 320 bps to 36.2%.

Initiatives: 42% or $131 million from SDN/NFV virtualizing 15% RAN, energy down 22%, VortexAI preempting outages, tech dispatches down 18%, OPEX/site $980. Europe $52 million savings, APAC 15% vendor cuts.

28% or $87 million SG&A: CAC $320 down 19%, churn 1.1%, dealer closures $41 million, LatAm hedges $22 million.

30% or $94 million media: sports renewals 11% lower, originals cut licensing 25%, ad-tier $68 million, EU locals $31 million.

Zero-based budgeting 85%, targeting opex/revenue sub-52%. Uplift drove EPS $0.78, FCF $2.3 billion, leverage 2.4x. Annualized $1.2 billion savings by 2025.

Regarding spectrum assets, we hold 520 MHz average depth: 160 MHz C-band, 120 MHz PCS, 80 MHz AWS-3, low-band/CBRS. Utilization 87% up from 78%. C-band 92% top MSAs 450 Mbps, low-band 82%, mmWave 65% urban rising to 95%, CBRS 78% media private nets. Northeast 94%, Sunbelt 89%, rural 72%. Traffic up 28% to 12.5 GB/user, <5% congestion via DSS.

Future plans: refarm 40 MHz legacy H2 boosting 25%, AI DSA 15% efficiency, slicing for 8K sports. $800 million auctions for mid-band to 600 MHz, FWA 80 MHz 2 million homes, private 100 MHz $500 million revenue, 6G R&D sub-THz. ROI to 35%.

On net subscriber additions, total 285,000 up 12% YoY: residential 235,000 up 15%, broadband +185,000 up 22% FTTH 15 million homes 28% take, wireless postpaid +95,000 up 10% 5G SA, video -20,000 offset by vMVPD +25,000. Business +50,000 up 18%: Ethernet +32,000, private 5G +12,000, SMB +6,000. AI bundles 65% attachment, guide Q4 220-250K residential, 45-55K business, FY >1.1 million.

Finally, network CapEx guidance FY2024 $12.8-13.6 billion or 18-19% revenue, 75% of total $17.2-18.2 billion. 5G SA $7.2-7.6 billion Ericsson/Nokia, Open RAN; fiber $3.4-3.7 billion XGS-PON 18 million locations BEAD $2.4 billion; edge/spectrum $2.2-2.3 billion 18,000 small cells. 2025 $12-13 billion. Strong returns 3-year payback, 92 Opensignal score.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high at over 99.99%. We are also improving rural coverage through dynamic spectrum sharing and FWA integrations.

Raj Singh: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter, up to 85 on NPS. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing enterprise penetration through private 5G and SD-WAN solutions.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on Open RAN, 6G precursors, and AI-driven orchestration.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding business net subscriber additions?

Raj Singh: Thanks for the question, John. Our business segment saw 50,000 net adds this quarter, up 18% year-over-year, driven by Ethernet growth of 32,000 and private 5G sites at 12,000. We're competing effectively with metro ring upgrades in data centers and URLLC for manufacturing, leveraging our converged portfolio to target sticky services like SASE, aiming for 20% revenue growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding operating expense management?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Emily. Inflation and rates are headwinds, but our opex program delivered $312 million savings, with AI maintenance cutting dispatches 18%, CAC down 19%, and content efficiencies. We're targeting sub-52% opex/revenue, supporting 8-10% EPS growth and leverage below peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Davis: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiencies in network operations?

Michael Reynolds: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core; we've reduced energy 22% via SDN/NFV and virtualized RAN, preempting outages with AI. Success metrics include opex/site reductions to $980, 99.99% uptime, and carbon targets tied to EU Gigabit goals and BEAD, tracking via annual ESG reports.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Michael, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Michael Reynolds: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in AetherLink Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
